outputs.L2: A system and process for identifying harmful substances in a consumable sample includes introducing the sample into a first compartment of a testing container and processing it to create a homogenized sample. The homogenized sample is then transferred to a second compartment having an outlet port. Within this second compartment, the homogenized sample is combined with a processing reagent to form a dispersion. A quantity of the dispersion is conveyed to an analysis compartment of the testing container. outputs.L3:
A consumable sample is first introduced into the first chamber of a test container. Within the container, the sample is processed into a homogenized form and transferred to a second chamber equipped with an outlet port. The homogenized sample is then mixed with a process reagent to produce a dispersion suitable for analysis.

A predetermined volume of the resulting dispersion is transmitted through the outlet port into an analysis chamber. This chamber contains a detection substrate positioned near the outlet port so that the dispersion can contact or interact with the substrate. An optical sensor monitors the detection substrate through a detection window and detects signals generated by the interaction. These signals indicate whether an allergen is present in the sample.
outputs.L4:
The system is designed to detect harmful substances, including allergens, contaminants, toxins, or other target analytes, in food, beverages, and similar consumable samples. Testing begins by placing a representative portion of the sample into a container that supports the principal preparation and analysis steps. The sample is homogenized, crushed, agitated, or otherwise processed to distribute any target substance throughout the sample material and produce a more uniform test portion.

A reagent is then introduced into the container and mixed with the homogenized sample. The reagent extracts or mobilizes the target substance and forms a liquid dispersion suitable for analysis. Depending on the application, the reagent may also include buffers, labeling agents, antibodies, or other compounds that promote a detectable reaction with the target analyte. Mixing may be performed manually or by an integrated mechanical mechanism to provide sufficient contact between the sample and reagent.

After preparation, at least part of the resulting dispersion is transferred to an analysis chamber within the same container. The transfer may occur through a channel, valve, filter, membrane, or other fluid-handling structure. Such components can help prevent large particles from entering the analysis chamber while allowing dissolved or suspended target substances to reach a detection substrate. The detection substrate may employ a colorimetric, fluorescent, immunological, or other optically readable assay. When the target allergen or harmful substance is present, a corresponding signal develops on or near the substrate.

An optical sensor observes the detection substrate through a transparent or optically accessible detection window. The sensor measures characteristics such as color intensity, fluorescence, reflectance, or signal location and compares the measured response with predetermined criteria. The system can then indicate whether the target substance is absent, present, or present above a specified threshold. Results may be displayed directly, transmitted to an external device, or stored for later review.

By combining sample homogenization, reagent mixing, fluid transfer, and optical detection in a single container, the system reduces the need for separate laboratory equipment and minimizes sample handling. This integrated arrangement can lower the risk of contamination, improve test consistency, and provide faster, more convenient safety screening at food-processing facilities, restaurants, retail locations, or points of consumption.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in formal patent language, a consumable-sample testing device with multiple chambers that processes a sample and optically detects harmful substances through a detection window.
counterfactuals.output:
**Exemplary Patent Description**

A consumable-sample testing device comprises a housing defining a plurality of fluidically interconnected chambers, including at least a sample-receiving chamber configured to receive a consumable sample, a processing chamber configured to condition the consumable sample, and a detection chamber configured to receive at least a portion of the conditioned consumable sample. The processing chamber contains, or is configured to receive, one or more reagents selected to extract, separate, concentrate, dilute, react with, or otherwise prepare a target substance present in the consumable sample.

The detection chamber includes an optically transmissive detection window disposed along an optical interrogation path. A detection reagent is provided within the detection chamber and is configured to produce an optically detectable response upon interaction with a harmful substance or an indicator thereof. An optical detector is positioned, or is positionable, relative to the detection window to transmit excitation light into the detection chamber and/or receive response light therefrom. The optically detectable response may comprise a change in absorbance, reflectance, transmittance, fluorescence, luminescence, color, or scattering.

At least one flow-control structure selectively controls movement of the consumable sample between the plurality of chambers. The flow-control structure may comprise a frangible seal, valve, capillary passage, porous membrane, movable barrier, pressure-actuated member, or combinations thereof. The housing may be configured as a single-use cartridge receivable by a reusable reader that includes the optical detector and a processor configured to determine, from an optical signal obtained through the detection window, the presence, absence, or concentration of the harmful substance.

**Exemplary Independent Claim**

1. A device for testing a consumable sample, the device comprising:  
   
   a housing defining a plurality of chambers, the plurality of chambers comprising:  
   
   a sample-receiving chamber configured to receive the consumable sample;  
   
   a processing chamber fluidically connectable to the sample-receiving chamber and configured to process at least a portion of the consumable sample; and  
   
   a detection chamber fluidically connectable to the processing chamber;  
   
   at least one reagent disposed within the housing and configured to interact with a harmful substance in the consumable sample, or with an indicator associated with the harmful substance, to generate an optically detectable response;  
   
   at least one flow-control structure configured to selectively permit transfer of the consumable sample between at least two of the plurality of chambers; and  
   
   an optically transmissive detection window forming at least a portion of the detection chamber and configured to permit optical interrogation of contents of the detection chamber,  
   
   wherein the device is configured such that an optical signal acquired through the detection window is usable to determine at least one of a presence, an absence, or a concentration of the harmful substance in the consumable sample.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.output: 1. **A test apparatus for detecting an allergen in a food sample by performing a testing method, the test apparatus comprising:** a test container defining a sample chamber configured to receive the food sample; a homogenizer operatively coupled to the sample chamber and configured to homogenize the food sample with a liquid to form a homogenate; a reagent chamber containing an allergen-detection reagent; a first fluid pathway configured to transfer at least a portion of the homogenate from the sample chamber to the reagent chamber for contact with the allergen-detection reagent to form a dispersion; an analysis chamber in fluid communication with the reagent chamber through a second fluid pathway and configured to receive at least a portion of the dispersion; an optical detector positioned to interrogate the dispersion in the analysis chamber; and a controller configured to cause the test apparatus to perform the testing method by operating the homogenizer, transferring the portion of the homogenate through the first fluid pathway into the reagent chamber, transferring the portion of the dispersion through the second fluid pathway into the analysis chamber, obtaining from the optical detector an optical measurement of the dispersion, and determining, based on the optical measurement, whether the allergen is present in the food sample.
